narrative:
On September 10, 2026, the Karnataka High Court scheduled 3,509 cases across 43 judges and heard 1,354, achieving an overall hearing rate of 38.6%. This marks a steady decline over recent sessions, falling from 44.2% on September 9 and 51.4% on September 8, primarily driven by a substantial surge in total scheduled volume compared to the 3,043 matters listed the previous day.

Individual courtroom throughput varied significantly based on docket size. High conversion rates were recorded in Hall 32 by Justice G. Basavaraja, who heard 83 of 113 listed cases (73.5%), and the Division Bench of Justice R. Devdas and Justice K. Manmadha Rao, which heard 51 of 76 matters (67.1%). In contrast, courts handling massive dockets experienced bottlenecks: Hall 15 under Justice Sachin Shankar Magadum heard 53 of 351 listed matters (15.1%), while a 279-case single cause list before Justice B. M. Shyam Prasad resulted in only 1 hearing.

Procedural stage analysis indicates that early-stage matters absorbed most judicial time. Admission matters converted at 46.5% (472 of 1,014 heard), while Orders dropped to 40.5% (409 of 1,011 heard), down from 58.1% on September 9. Final Hearing conversion remained modest at 30.3%, whereas Further Hearings saw severe gridlock, converting only 5.5% (22 of 401 matters). 

Writ Petitions constituted the largest volume by case type, with 1,428 matters listed and 499 heard (34.9%), reflecting a continued contraction in conversion from 38.5% yesterday and 52.9% on September 8. Criminal Petitions saw 222 of 496 matters heard (44.8%), while Miscellaneous First Appeals converted at 50.1%. Criminal Appeals demonstrated strong clearance efficiency, with 70.2% heard (106 of 151), offsetting weaker progress in Company Applications, which cleared just 3.7% of its 187 scheduled matters.
